title: 102 Flirty Questions to Ask a Boy (Cute, Fun and Tasteful)
h1: 102 Flirty Questions to Ask a Boy: Cute, Playful and Tasteful
description: Try these 102 flirty questions to ask a boy: cute, playful and tasteful picks for texting or in person, plus tips on reading his reaction well.
keyword: flirty questions to ask a boy
excerpt: 102 flirty questions to ask a boy, from cute openers and texting questions to would-you-rather picks, plus tips on reading his reaction.
intro:
Flirting with a boy you like doesn't have to mean rehearsed lines or awkward silences. Sometimes all it takes is one playful question that makes him grin, blush or fire back something just as cheeky. The right question tells him you're interested without spelling it out, and it gives you both a reason to keep talking.

Below are 102 flirty questions to ask a boy, all tasteful and nothing explicit. They're grouped by mood: light and cute, perfect for texting, about his crush on you, would-you-rather style, a little bolder and deeper flirty questions for when the spark is clearly there. After the lists, you'll find tips on reading his reaction, keeping things respectful and flirting smoothly over text.
body:
Light and cute flirty questions

These are easygoing openers that hint at interest without putting anyone on the spot. They're ideal when you're just starting to talk. Ask one or two at a time, toss in your own answer and save the bolder sections for when he's clearly flirting back.

Tip: Delivery is half the flirt. A smile, a raised eyebrow or a well-placed winking emoji turns an ordinary question into an obviously playful one.
  1. What's the cutest thing anyone has ever done to get your attention?
  2. Do you blush easily, or are you a professional at hiding it?
  3. What's your most charming quality, in your own humble opinion?
  4. Are you a hand-holder or a pinky-link kind of guy?
  5. What's your go-to move when you want to make someone smile?
  6. Be honest: how long do you spend getting ready before you see someone you like?
  7. What nickname would you secretly love to be called?
  8. Do you think you're a good dancer, or just a confident one?
  9. What's the smoothest thing you've ever said that actually worked?
  10. Which of your smiles is the real one: the polite one or the goofy one?
  11. Do you believe in lucky shirts? Do you own one?
  12. What's the sweetest compliment a stranger has ever given you?
  13. Would you rather get a handwritten note or a playlist made just for you?
  14. What's a song that makes you want to slow dance in the kitchen?
  15. If you had to describe your flirting style as a weather forecast, what would it be?
  16. Are you more likely to send the first text or wait for one?
  17. What tiny gesture instantly wins you over?
  18. Do you get butterflies, or are you too cool for that?

Flirty questions to ask a boy over text

Texting gives you time to be clever, and it gives him time to come up with something cute in return. These questions are made for the chat window. For more conversation starters, see our guide on how to start a conversation with a guy over text.

  1. What were you doing right before you saw my message?
  2. Okay, real talk: did you smile when my name popped up?
  3. Which emoji best describes your mood when you talk to me?
  4. What's one thing you'd say to me right now if you weren't being shy?
  5. Are you the type to reread a conversation you enjoyed?
  6. Describe your ideal hangout with me in three emojis.
  7. What's the last thing that made you think of me?
  8. Voice note or text: which do you want from me next?
  9. If I called you right now, would you pick up or panic first?
  10. Who's going to say goodnight first tonight, you or me?
  11. Rate my texting game from one to ten. Be gentle.
  12. What's a song you'd send me if you wanted to drop a hint?
  13. Would you rather I send you a good-morning text or a goodnight text?
  14. What would you have said in your first message if you'd been totally brave?
  15. Are you smiling at your phone right now? Don't lie.
  16. What's your honest reaction when I leave you on read for five minutes?
  17. If our text thread had a title, what would it be?
  18. Do you screenshot conversations you like, or is that just me?

Questions about his crush on you

Once you're fairly sure the interest is mutual, these questions let him admit it in a playful way. If you're still not sure, read up on the signs in does my crush like me first.

  1. What did you think the first time we talked?
  2. Was there a moment you realized you liked talking to me more than you expected?
  3. Have you ever planned a conversation with me in your head?
  4. What's something about me you'd like to know but haven't asked?
  5. Do you remember what I was wearing the day we met?
  6. What's the most attractive thing about my personality?
  7. Have you ever bragged about me to your friends?
  8. What do your friends say when my name comes up?
  9. Did you ever try to casually run into me on purpose?
  10. What's one thing I do that you find ridiculously cute?
  11. Would you tell me if you had a crush on me, or would I have to guess?
  12. What's a word you'd use to describe me to someone who's never met me?
  13. When we hang out, what's the part you look forward to most?
  14. Is there anything you've been waiting for the right moment to tell me?
  15. Do I make you nervous? Just a little?
  16. What would our first proper date look like if you planned it?
  17. What's something I said that you keep thinking about?
  18. If you could rewind to any moment we've shared, which one would you pick?

Flirty would-you-rather questions

Would-you-rather questions are low pressure because he's choosing between two options rather than confessing anything. Both answers still tell you something. Want more? Try our would you rather questions for couples.

  1. Would you rather go on a picnic date or a rooftop dinner date?
  2. Would you rather I steal your hoodie or your fries?
  3. Would you rather have a slow dance at a wedding or a silly dance at a concert?
  4. Would you rather get a surprise kiss on the cheek or a surprise hug from behind?
  5. Would you rather stargaze with me or watch the sunrise with me?
  6. Would you rather be the big spoon or the little spoon?
  7. Would you rather I serenade you badly in public or write you a cheesy poem?
  8. Would you rather lose to me at mini golf or beat me and deal with my pouting?
  9. Would you rather spend a rainy day with me indoors or go splash in puddles?
  10. Would you rather get matching couple shirts or matching friendship bracelets?
  11. Would you rather I laugh at all your jokes or tease you about them?
  12. Would you rather have a whole day of my undivided attention or a surprise visit when you least expect it?
  13. Would you rather plan a date for me or have me plan one for you?
  14. Would you rather share an umbrella or share headphones?
  15. Would you rather I text you a cheesy pickup line every morning or call you every night?
  16. Would you rather have our first kiss be totally spontaneous or perfectly planned?

A little bolder (but still PG-13)

Save these for when the flirting is clearly mutual. They turn up the heat a notch while keeping things classy, so he can answer as boldly or as bashfully as he likes.

  1. What's the most flirtatious thing you've ever done in public?
  2. Do you prefer someone who makes the first move, or do you like making it?
  3. What's the most attractive thing someone can say to you?
  4. What's the best kiss you've ever seen in a movie?
  5. Where would you take me if you wanted to impress me?
  6. What's a compliment you'd love to hear from me?
  7. Do you think we'd be good at keeping a secret together?
  8. What's the most daring thing you'd do on a date?
  9. Are you more attracted to confidence or a little bit of mystery?
  10. If I held your hand right now, what would you do?
  11. Have you ever thought about what it would be like to kiss me?
  12. What's one thing you'd want to do on our first date that you'd never admit to your friends?
  13. Would you rather I flirt with you subtly or make it completely obvious?
  14. What does someone have to do to give you real butterflies?
  15. Do you like being teased, or would you rather do the teasing?
  16. What's your favorite feature of mine? You only get to pick one.

Deeper flirty questions

Flirting isn't only about teasing. These questions mix romance with real curiosity, which is often what turns a crush into something more. If you're already dating, our list of deep questions to ask your boyfriend goes even further.

  1. What makes you feel instantly comfortable with someone?
  2. What's something you're looking for that you haven't found in anyone yet?
  3. Do you think chemistry is something you feel right away or something that grows?
  4. What's the most romantic thing about you that most people never see?
  5. What do you think makes a crush turn into something real?
  6. When you like someone, how do you show it?
  7. What kind of attention makes you feel the most special?
  8. What's something that makes you feel safe opening up to someone?
  9. Do you think we'd make a good team? Why?
  10. What's a quality you hope the person you date sees in you?
  11. Have you ever had a feeling about someone from the very first conversation?
  12. What's one memory you'd like to make with someone you really like?
  13. What's the difference between someone you have fun with and someone you fall for?
  14. What would make you want to slow down and really get to know someone?
  15. What's a romantic gesture you've always wanted to try?
  16. How would you want someone to tell you they like you?

How to read his reaction

His response tells you a lot about whether the flirting is landing. Look for the overall pattern rather than a single answer.

  • Good signs: he answers with enthusiasm, asks you the same question back, adds his own teasing, keeps the conversation going or brings up something you said earlier.
  • Mixed signals: short but friendly replies can mean he's shy, busy or unsure how to flirt back. Give it a little time and try a lighter question.
  • Signs to ease off: one-word answers, changing the subject, long gaps every time things turn flirty or a polite "haha" with nothing else. That's your cue to dial it back to friendly.

In person, body language helps too: a real smile, steady eye contact and leaning in are encouraging. Our guide to signs he secretly likes you through body language covers more cues.

Keeping it respectful and consensual

Good flirting makes both people feel good. It should never make anyone feel cornered.

  • Match his energy. If he's playful, keep going. If he seems uncomfortable, switch to something neutral without making it awkward.
  • Let him skip questions. "Pass" is always a valid answer, and laughing it off keeps the mood light.
  • Keep it tasteful. Bold doesn't mean explicit. Anything sexual should only come up once you both clearly want it, in a relationship where you trust each other.
  • Don't use answers against him. If he admits he was nervous around you, that's sweet, not ammunition for teasing in front of friends.
  • Respect a no. If he isn't interested, accept it gracefully. Being kind about it says a lot about you.
Tip: If you're both under 18, keep flirting light and age-appropriate, and never feel pressured to send photos or say anything you're not comfortable with.

Texting tips for flirty conversations

  • Don't double-text a flirty question. If he hasn't answered yet, wait. Pressure kills the playful mood.
  • Use emojis sparingly. One wink or smirk signals your tone; five feels like a puzzle.
  • Answer your own question. "Would you rather share an umbrella or share headphones? I'm team headphones" gives him an easy reply.
  • Mix in compliments. A specific, sincere compliment pairs well with a flirty question.
  • Move it offline. If the texting is great, suggest meeting up. Chemistry is easier to read face to face.
  • Know when to say goodnight. Ending on a high note keeps him looking forward to the next chat.

Running low on topics? Our list of things to talk about with your crush can keep things flowing.

The bottom line

The best flirty questions are light, a little cheeky and asked with a smile. Start with cute ones, pay attention to how he responds and only turn up the heat when he's clearly enjoying it. Most of all, have fun with it. Flirting is a way to show someone you like their company, and the right question makes that easy to say without saying it outright.
takeaways: Start with light, cute questions and only get bolder once he's clearly flirting back.
Answer your own questions so flirting feels like a fun back-and-forth.
Enthusiastic replies and questions asked back are good signs; short, deflecting answers mean ease off.
Keep it tasteful and respect any question he'd rather skip.
Over text, send one question at a time and suggest meeting up when the chemistry is there.

faq.q: What are some flirty questions to ask a boy?
faq.a: Try playful questions like: Big spoon or little spoon? Did you smile when my name popped up? What's one thing I do that you find cute? Would you rather stargaze with me or watch the sunrise with me? Keep them light, add your own answer and see how he responds before getting bolder.

faq.q: How do you flirt with a boy over text?
faq.a: Send one playful question at a time, add your own answer and use an emoji or two to set the tone. Mix in sincere compliments, don't double-text if he's slow to reply and end the conversation on a high note. If the chat is going well, suggest meeting in person.

faq.q: How do I know if a boy is flirting back?
faq.a: He's likely flirting back if he answers with enthusiasm, asks you the same question, teases you playfully, keeps the conversation going and remembers details you've shared. One-word replies or quickly changing the subject usually mean he's not interested or not comfortable, so ease off.

faq.q: What should you not ask a boy when flirting?
faq.a: Avoid explicit or sexual questions early on, questions that compare him to others, and anything that feels like a test or a trap. Skip heavy topics like past breakups until you know each other well. If a question could make him feel cornered, save it for later or leave it out.
